newsitem.title: SPAIN: Opposition questions Spain govt's 1997 forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Opposition questions Spain govt's 1997 forecasts.

text.p: The Spanish government's economic growth forecasts for 1997 are not credible, spokesman for the Socialist opposition party Juan Eguiagaray said on Wednesday.
"It is not credible that the Spanish economy can continue growing at three percent," Eguiagaray told a parliamentary committee.
On Monday, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro reaffirmed the government's three percent GDP growth forecast for 1997.
Eguiagaray said weakness in other European countries, particularly Germany, would stop Spain meeting the target this year.
The opposition, ousted from power by the Popular Party last March, also doubted how the 1996 public deficit target had been reached given the "disastrous" performance of the cash deficit, he added.
Last week, the government announced that the 1996 public deficit was 3.3 percent of GDP, under-shooting the government's 3.5 percent target.
